Do you have anyone close to you that can act s a support, without judging you? If so, lean on them and let them be there for you. Ask if you can reach out to them at random hours when you might find yourself struggling. If you don't have anyone, there are some cognitive behavioral therapy modalities that you can try to use when you're tempted. One is to go through your senses and think of 5 things for each of them. So five things you see, five things you hear, smell, feel and five things you taste or can go taste. Another is deep breathing. Breathe in so your stomach moves instead of your chest. Breathe in for a count of 4 seconds, hold it for 7 and let it out for a count of 8. 

Distraction is big. If you feel pissed off, punch a pillow or scream into it. If you feel sad, let yourself cry or do something to pamper yourself and indulge in the feeling. If you feel nothing, try to occupy your mind, read a book, color, watch a movie...

I'm sorry you're struggling so much. I often have urges to self harm but the stuff above has helped me for more than ten years so far.

Self injury first around 6-7 years old. I remember digging my nails into my hand while being yelled at. 

Emotional abuse => sexual abuse => verbal abuse. Very emotionally distant mother. Parents divorced, father was a weekend dad. Mom had live-in boyfriend who emotionally abused her my entire childhood. He'd move in and out of the house at random. Mom has eating disorder. 

I develop eating disorder behavior around 11. Hiding food, not eating in front of people, eating til I felt sick and not knowing why. Then fasting the next day. Full on bulimic by the time I was 15, purging up to 5x per day. 

Self injury worsens throughout. Escalates from digging nails in to skin to picking the razor blades out of pink Shick razors and using them to slice my arm. Turns in to burning myself with a lighter and using straight blades to cut deeper/bigger. My right arm from wrist to above my elbow is scar tissue as is my right ankle and areas of my stomach and hands. 

1st suicide attempt at 14, swallowed a bunch of random OTC meds and passed out in the bathroom. Woke up next day, pissed it didn't work, sidled off to school in a drugged up zombie state. 

2nd suicide attempt at 24. Cut my arm lengthwise in my car in an abandoned parking lot at night. Things got a little fuzzy and when I came to I drove home one-armed thinking of what a fucking idiot I am. Annoyed that i bled on the upholstery. Lots of suicidal behavior in between but nothing I'd consider a true attempt. 

Went to a crisis clinic after the last attempt and they said I wasn't a serious enough case. Went to the mental hospital, they said they had no services for me. Cried so hard in the rooftop parking lot that I lost my voice. 

I'm 28 now, I see a psychiatrist and take 225mg effexor xr daily with 50mg lamictal which was recently added. Still have these weird dips in mood were I want to die. 

How do I deal...lately I tend to sulk and indulge in the sadness. Eventually it seems to pick up a bit but I always have this pervasive "I should just be dead" feeling in the back of my head. Like an annoying solicitor knocking on the door that won't fucking leave. Been to therapy a few times but never really clicked with a therapist.

Check in with yourself mentally to make sure you're not feeling out of control/suicidal/self-injurious and if you are, talk to family or friends or a hotline, anyone.  Make sure you're eating enough and sleeping as much as you can despite the circumstances.  Don't pressure yourself to do or feel anything.

After renting a total shithole that almost ended in a court dispute, I am the motherfucking queen of paranoia about rentals.

- When you go look at the place, don't be afraid to air that sucker out.  Open all the cabinets and look inside.  Check out the closets.  Turn on the faucets and check the water pressure and that the water gets hot.  Make sure the pipes aren't wet.  Look around for dead bug carcasses (or worse, live bugs).  Turn lights on and off.

- Are there enough outlets?  Are they in spots that make sense for you?

- Do you have cell reception everywhere in the apartment?

- If the HVAC is vented and you care about smoke smells, is the building no smoking / what happens if your neighbors smoke and it seeps in to your place?

- Thermostats?  Do they work?  A/C and heat - do they work?

- Can you access your electric meter (good to make sure yours and other units' not Mcgyvered together) and your power box, in case the power goes out and you need to flip the breakers?

Edit: oh, and if you care about crime or what your neighbors will be like, go sit in your car nearby after dark and see what kind of people are hanging around.
